Run from packages/gateway (pnpm --filter @theokit/gateway run test:mutation); deliberately NOT wired into `test`, so `pnpm -r run test` in CI never pays for it. configFile points at vitest.mutation.config.ts, which drops tests/lint/** — those suites walk the monorepo tree from the repo root (__dirname/../../../..) and break inside Stryker's sandbox, and they READ source text rather than executing it, so they could never kill a mutant of these two files anyway. related:false because tests live in a mirror tree (tests/**) and vitest --related cannot map a source file back to them. inPlace is deliberately unset: the sandbox works once the lint suites are excluded, and the working tree is never mutated in place. mutate is scoped to the two files with real branching logic that only unit tests cover — both chunkers and the hook chain; src/hooks/types.ts is types-only and has nothing to mutate. thresholds.break=93 is the MEASURED baseline with headroom for one mutant (93.35% on 2026-08-29; one mutant is 0.25% of 406). READ THIS BEFORE COMPARING IT TO AN OLDER NUMBER: it is not a drop from the 94.35% recorded earlier the same day. That figure was over TWO files; this one is over four, and the two added arrived with 65 survivors between them. Scoring less of the code higher is not a better suite, so the scope moved and the floor moved with it -- which is the one case where lowering break is honest, and it is honest only because the change is stated here. It makes the score a ratchet: a real regression fails the run, with roughly one mutant of headroom. Only the killed/timeout split moved between runs, and a timeout scores as killed. Raise break when the score rises; never lower it to make a red run green.

thresholds.break=95 is the MEASURED baseline (95.63% on 2026-08-29) with headroom for three mutants of 0.22% each. It has been raised three times in one day and lowered once, and the once matters: it went 93 -> 87 when the scope grew from two files to four, because the two added arrived with 65 survivors between them. Scoring less of the code higher is not a better suite, so the floor follows the scope -- the only case where lowering it is honest, and honest only because it is written here. Raise it when the score rises; never lower it to make a red run green under an UNCHANGED scope.

All 20 remaining survivors are equivalent mutants -- none of them changes behaviour, so no test can kill one and a test that appeared to would be measuring something else. They are enumerated with the reason for each in tests/MUTATION.md. Anything NOT on that list is outstanding work.
